catalogue.authority: The committed catalogue is the authority for a live factor's id, label, group, role and status. This register adds the extracted detail behind each factor and is refused if it contradicts the catalogue.

horizon.end: 05:00 Europe/London on the next local date
horizon.note: One 24-hour session whose two ends are London wall-clock times one local date apart. The first statement of this target was 05:00 London to 17:00 America/New_York on the same local date; it was withdrawn on 2026-10-14 and anything still carrying it is superseded. A session starts on a Monday-to-Friday local date only: the London spring (01:00Z, last Sunday of March) and autumn (01:00Z, last Sunday of October) transitions fall inside the session that starts on the preceding Saturday, so that start measures 23 hours in spring and 25 in autumn and is not a session. The Friday session therefore contains Friday's US close and ends on Saturday morning, which is intended. Every eligible session is exactly 24 hours, held by test over every Monday-to-Friday start from 2023 to 2027 (backtester/tests/usd_session_engine_interface.test.js).

target.rule: No intraday DXY print exists in this repository or in the live collector, so the label instrument and the quote source are unverified at both ends. If a claim is really about EUR/USD, a custom basket or any other instrument, name that instrument and say so; never present another instrument as DXY. The live collector prices the dollar with FRED DTWEXBGS, which is a feature and cannot be the session label: H.10 publishes on Mondays at 16:15 ET for the previous business week, so at a 05:00 London cutoff that value is 2 to 6 business days old (median 4).

weights.rulebook_source: logic/agent_usd_direction.md v2.1, which the live workflow fetches from GitHub on every run; the two vectors and the disagreements between them are catalogued in docs/research/usd-session/v1/weight_vector_discrepancy.md

aggregation.formula: conviction = round(winning side weight / active weight * 100), where active weight is the sum of the bullish and bearish weights only
steps: Each factor returns a signal of BULLISH, BEARISH or NEUTRAL with an evidence string and a reason.
The timeframe's coded weight is added to the pile of the signal that returned; a NEUTRAL factor's weight goes to the neutral pile and never to active weight.
bullish_argument_pct = round(bullish weight / active weight * 100), and bearish_argument_pct the same on the bearish side.
The direction is the heavier side; an exact tie returns NO_CLEAR_BIAS.
A direction whose absolute net edge is below 20 is published with the suffix _LEAN.
conviction is the winning side's percentage of active weight, and 0 when the direction is NO_CLEAR_BIAS.
verdict_strength is bucketed from the absolute net edge: 40 or more VERY_STRONG, 25 or more STRONG, 15 or more MODERATE, otherwise WEAK.
consequences: A missing input cannot lower conviction: its weight leaves active weight, so conviction is a share of the evidence that arrived and can read 100 while half the weight is absent.
neutral_pct is a sum of weight points printed with a per-cent sign in the reason string, not a percentage of anything.
NO_CLEAR_BIAS requires an exact tie of the two weight sums, so abstention is an arithmetic accident rather than a designed gate.

modifiers.note: logic/agent_usd_direction.md sections 8.2 to 8.5 describe a participation cap, a missing-input penalty, a conflict penalty and an agreement boost. The conviction node implements none of them and returns the rulebook's own names as fixed values, so no published call can have been moved by any of the four.

values.participation: the active weight in points, identical to participation_cap
values.participation_cap: the active weight in points, so no capacity is ever withheld
values.weighted_edge: the absolute net edge divided by 100

modifiers.source: exports/usd_layer1_agent.json -> Calculate USD Conviction, conviction_model legacy aliases

defects: Two weight vectors are live at once: the workflow fetches the rulebook on every run while the code uses its own constants, so the published number follows the code. F7 carries 24 coded points against a rulebook weight of 3 and F8 12 against 18, and nothing reconciles them.

The F7 signal string is produced outside the reachable workflow, so 24 of the 100 coded points cannot be reproduced from this repository: every node in the collector export that could compute a surprise from a calendar is an entry point with no consumer.

'Code | Derive Fed Bias' is a second implementation of the bias score with no consumer, and the collector's own data_quality note names it as the source of the live fed_bias, which is in fact computed by 'Code | Derive USD Eco Inputs'.
The same data_quality note says latest_us_event is selected from the Finnhub economic calendar, while the live row is read from Supabase and the Finnhub chain never reaches the snapshot.

The helpers latestUsEventFromEcoData and upcomingEventsFromEcoData, which would recompute the event signal from actual against forecast and invert the sign for Unemployment Rate and Initial Jobless Claims, are defined and never called.

The four modifiers of rulebook section 8 are returned as constants: participation and participation_cap equal the active weight, and conflict_penalty, missing_input_penalty and agreement_boost are all zero.
neutral_pct is a sum of weight points reported with a per-cent sign inside the reason string.

Snapshot selection is sortedRows.find(isUsableUsdSnapshot) || sortedRows[0]: it has no as-of bound against the 05:00 London cutoff, no per-field age and no revision exclusion, and the fallback row may be missing inputs the pack requires.
Gold, BTC and NQ history percentages count stored collector rows, so those lookbacks follow the pipeline's run history rather than a trading calendar.
Fields exist in the stored row and are written as null on every run: spx_d1_pct, btc_dominance, latest_ez_event, ecb_bias, global_growth_regime, ez_stress_flag and geopolitical_risk_flag.
equities_regime is computed from the 16 and 25 VIX thresholds, stored in the row and exposed to the model, and read by no conviction factor, which recomputes the regime from vix_level.

WTI, Brent and the five FX pairs are fetched and transformed in the collector but are not first-class fields of the stored snapshot; they survive only inside raw_payload, with the US-DE 10Y and US-JP 10Y spreads.
The dashboard publishes a second strength label derived separately from the same call, so two strength labels can disagree on one row.

The label instrument and its quote source are still undecided: the collector prices the dollar with FRED DTWEXBGS, a weekly broad H.10 index 2 to 6 business days old at a 05:00 London cutoff, and no intraday dollar-index print exists in the repository or the collector.

factors.label: F3 US-DE 2Y spread delta
factors.definition: The five-day change in the US minus German 2-year yield spread, read as the relative-rate stance behind the dollar; the deployed code reads one fixed five-day change at every timeframe, and the rulebook factor is the same spread delta with the same thresholds.

inputs.source: computed in the collector from FRED DGS2 (node 'HTTP Request | US 2Y Treasury Yield - FRED API') and a Bundesbank CSV German 2Y node ('HTTP Request | Germany 2Y Yield'), stored by the USD collector
inputs.transform: five-day difference of the spread level
inputs.cutoff: inherits the older leg; the German CSV and the US close are 1 to 2 business days old at 05:00 London

factors.rule: At or above +5 bps reads BULLISH, at or below -5 bps BEARISH, otherwise NEUTRAL, on one fixed five-day window. Threshold +/- 5 bps. Coded weight 10, rulebook weight 16.
factors.missing_stale: A missing spread delta scores NEUTRAL and names the missing input; the input pack also lists `de_2y_yield`, `us_de_2y_spread` and `us_de_2y_spread_d5_bps` as must-be-neutral if unavailable. factors.historical_availability: The US leg is in the closed study's cache from 2023-04-03 and in the 22-series macro frame from 2024-01-02; the Bundesbank German 2Y series was not traced in either cached frame in this cycle.

factors.label: F5 DXY delta
factors.definition: The percentage change in the dollar index the collector stores as `dxy_level`, read as confirmation that the market is already expressing dollar strength or weakness; the code reads a 1-day change on 24h with a tighter threshold and a 5-day or 20-day change on the longer timeframes.

inputs.source: collected by the USD collector node 'HTTP Request | DXY - FRED Dollar Index - FRED API' and turned into percentage changes by fredPct (offsets of 1, 5 and 20 observations of the returned series); target_source_assessment.md records the stored series as FRED DTWEXBGS, the Federal Reserve H.10 nominal broad U.S. dollar index, not the ICE DXY basket, and the source page states that all values are subject to revision
inputs.units: per cent change of the index level
inputs.transform: percentage change over 1, 5 or 20 observations of the series
inputs.lookback: 1 day on 24h; 5 days on 3d and current_week; 20 days on next_week and current_month when dxy_d20 is present
inputs.cutoff: 2 to 6 business days old at 05:00 London, median 4, because the H.10 family is released on Mondays at 16:15 ET for the previous business week

factors.rule: On 24h: at or above +0.15 per cent BULLISH, at or below -0.15 per cent BEARISH, otherwise NEUTRAL. On every other timeframe: +/- 0.30 per cent. Coded weight 14 on 24h, rulebook weight 6.
factors.missing_stale: A missing delta scores NEUTRAL and names the missing input. The substitutions are silent and one of them changes the test: on 24h a null `dxy_d1` moves the factor to `dxy_d5` while the threshold stays at the 1-day 0.15 per cent, so a five-day move is judged on the tighter band, and on the two long timeframes a null `dxy_d20` moves it to `dxy_d5`. Neither substitution reaches the numeric payload.
dependencies: A dollar index whose release schedule is daily rather than weekly, and a decision on which index the label instrument uses.
factors.overlap: The collected series is a broad dollar index, so whenever the session label is built from the same index family the factor contains part of the target; it also restates F2, F3 and F4 as a price rather than as a yield, and the rulebook makes it the primary tiebreaker, a role the code never grants it.
factors.historical_availability: FRED DTWEXBGS is a daily series available well before the closed study's cache (2023-04-03) and the macro frame (2024-01-02); latest published values only, no vintage, so revisions are invisible.
factors.live_availability: One collector row per day at the 09:30 ET pipeline time and no per-field age, so the newest observation is already several business days old at the 05:00 London cutoff.

factors.label: F6 Gold delta
factors.definition: The change in the spot gold price, read as the anti-dollar leg: gold weakness is scored as dollar support and gold strength as dollar pressure; the deployed code inverts the sign against a 0.1 per cent band, and the rulebook states the same inversion without a numeric band.

inputs.source: Coinbase spot quote collected by the node 'HTTP Request | Gold - Coinbase'; the percentage changes are computed by the collector's historyPct against its own previously stored snapshot rows ('Supabase | Get Previous Market Snapshots'), so the window is counted in stored pipeline rows rather than in calendar days or exchange sessions
inputs.transform: percentage change against the row 1, 5 or 20 positions back in the collector's own history, with a fallback to the 1-day column when the 5-day column is missing
inputs.lookback: 5 stored rows on 24h, 3d and current_week; 20 stored rows on next_week and current_month when gold_d20_pct is present, otherwise the 5-row arm
inputs.cutoff: spot quote read at the 09:30 ET pipeline time, so the observed price is not a 05:00 London print and no as-of check is applied

factors.rule: Gold below -0.1 per cent reads BULLISH, gold above +0.1 per cent BEARISH, inside +/- 0.1 per cent NEUTRAL, on the selected lookback. Coded weight 4 on 24h, rulebook weight 5.
factors.missing_stale: A missing gold delta scores NEUTRAL and names the missing input; the input pack silently substitutes `gold_d1_pct` for a missing `gold_d5_pct` and records only a warning string, so a one-row move can be labelled and scored as a five-day move, and the row counts themselves depend on how often the collector ran.
dependencies: A gold price series with a fixed daily benchmark time, and a window counted in calendar or session time rather than in pipeline rows.
factors.overlap: F4 already reads the real-rate complex from the other side, and F1, F9 and F10 read the same risk appetite through VIX and equities; when gold and the dollar rise together the rulebook tells the model to flag a safe-haven conflict, while the code carries a conflict penalty that is hard-coded to zero.
factors.historical_availability: A Coinbase spot price is retrievable historically, but the closed study's cache and the macro frame record no gold series traced in this cycle, so the row-based window has no obvious historical equivalent.
factors.live_availability: One quote per collector run, no vintage, no benchmark time, and the deltas are only as regular as the pipeline's run history.

factors.label: F7 US economic surprise
factors.definition: The dollar-side read of the most recent completed US release: the collector stores a per-event signal string and the conviction node copies that string; the magnitude of the surprise, the consensus it was measured against and the event's age are never read.

inputs.source: the event row the collector stores ('Supabase | Get Today USD Economic Events'), passed through 'Code | Derive USD Eco Inputs' to 'Normalise Market Snapshot'; the string is one of BULLISH, BEARISH or NEUTRAL and its producer is not reachable in the collector export, because every node that would compute it from a calendar ('HTTP Request | Eco Calendar Recent - Finnhub', 'HTTP Request | Eco Calendar Upcoming - Finnhub', 'Code | Process Eco Data', 'Code | Derive Fed Bias') is an entry point with no consumer in this workflow
inputs.transform: none; the string is scored as it is stored
inputs.lookback: the single latest completed event the row carries, whatever its age
inputs.cutoff: no as-of check; the stored event also carries date and time fields that the signal rule never reads

factors.rule: BULLISH reads BULLISH (positive US surprise supports USD), BEARISH reads BEARISH, any other string or a missing event reads NEUTRAL. No threshold, no surprise magnitude. Coded weight 24 on 24h, 8 on 3d, 5 on current_week, 6 on next_week, 5 on current_month; rulebook weight 3 inside a 72-hour window.
factors.missing_stale: A null `latest_us_event` scores NEUTRAL with the evidence string 'No recent US event'. The collector also appends latest_us_event to the snapshot's missing array and marks source_status partial, but the agent end sees only the null, so a partial row and a healthy row produce the same factor reading. A stale event is indistinguishable from a fresh one: nothing holds the rulebook's 72-hour window, and neither a consensus revision nor a first print is detectable.
dependencies: A consensus forecast archive with a first-print vintage, so that a surprise magnitude can be formed and dated.
factors.overlap: A release moves the same rates and price inputs that F2, F4 and F5 read, so one surprise can enter the score three or four times; F8 is derived from the same stored event rows and F9 reads the same regime.
factors.historical_availability: No consensus or first-print archive is committed. The calendar in the closed study's data records release times without consensus values and an ALFRED vintage file needs a key, so a historical surprise series cannot be rebuilt from this repository.
factors.live_availability: One row per day, with an event date and time stored but never tested for age, and no vintage of either the consensus or the stored string.

factors.label: F8 Fed bias
factors.definition: The stored Fed-bias string, tested for the words hawkish or dovish, read as the direction of policy expectations. The rulebook factor is the change in bias; only the current string is retained, so no change can be measured, and the code tests the absolute state the rulebook says not to trade.

inputs.source: computed inside the collector by 'Code | Derive USD Eco Inputs' from the last eight completed events of the stored calendar: plus one for a BULLISH usd_signal and minus one for a BEARISH one, doubled when the event's impact rank is three, summed and labelled hawkish at two or more, dovish at minus two or less, neutral otherwise. A second implementation in the same export, 'Code | Derive Fed Bias', would score the same events plus or minus one; that node has no consumer and never runs
inputs.transform: substring test for hawkish and for dovish
inputs.cutoff: no as-of check; the string is recomputed once per collector run from whichever completed events the stored calendar holds

factors.rule: A string containing 'hawkish' reads BULLISH, one containing 'dovish' BEARISH, neutral NEUTRAL, 'unknown' is treated as a missing input and scores NEUTRAL. No threshold, no comparison against a prior reading. Coded weight 12 on 24h, 10 on 3d, 12 on current_week, 18 on next_week, 18 on current_month; rulebook weight 18, described there as the highest-weight factor and explicitly a delta.
factors.missing_stale: An absent or 'unknown' string scores NEUTRAL and names the missing input. The two-point cutoff behind the string is a coded constant with no stated calibration, the eight-event window is undocumented, and because only the current string survives, no amount of stored data can show whether the bias changed since the previous session.
dependencies: A retained vintage of the bias string, or of the events behind it, so that a change in bias can be measured.
factors.overlap: F7 is built from the same stored event rows and contributes to the same score, F2 and F4 read the same policy path through yields, and F9 uses this string as a gate, so one policy story can carry five factors.
factors.historical_availability: No fed_bias series appears in the closed study's data or in the 22-series macro frame, and the events behind the score are not archived with consensus values, so the factor has no history to test as specified.
factors.live_availability: One string per collector run, no vintage, no stored score as evidence, and no age attached to the events inside it.

factors.label: F9 Dollar Smile regime
factors.definition: The Dollar Smile read of the regime: the dollar is expected to be bid at the two extremes of the smile and offered in the middle, so the deployed rule looks for a high-volatility regime or for a calm regime whose bias string is not hawkish. The rulebook's bullish left side, US growth outperforming global growth with a hawkish Fed, has no input in the code.

inputs.source: FRED VIXCLS through the collector's vix_level field and the collector-derived fed_bias string
inputs.transform: level comparisons at 25 and 16 plus a substring test for hawkish
inputs.lookback: levels only; no change in VIX and no change in bias is read, although the rulebook lists vix_d1 and vix_d5
inputs.cutoff: inherits both inputs: VIXCLS is a market-close series and the bias string is recomputed once per collector run

factors.rule: VIX above 25 reads BULLISH; VIX below 16 while the bias string does not contain 'hawkish' reads BEARISH; every other case NEUTRAL. Coded weight 1 on 24h, 3 on 3d, 5 on current_week, 10 on next_week, 10 on current_month; rulebook weight 12.
factors.missing_stale: A missing VIX level returns NEUTRAL with the evidence string 'No clear Dollar Smile edge', which is the same answer the factor gives whenever VIX sits between 16 and 25 or the bias string is unknown, so a missing input and an uninformative regime are indistinguishable in the payload. The rulebook's permission to score NEUTRAL to avoid double-counting F1 is not implemented as a test.
dependencies: A verified publication time for VIXCLS, a retained vintage of the bias string, and a growth measure for the smile's left side.
factors.overlap: F1 applies the same 25 and 16 thresholds to the same VIX level, F10 gates on them again, and F8 reads the same bias string, so this factor adds only the 'not hawkish' test on top of F1 on the timeframe where both are scored.
factors.historical_availability: VIXCLS is reachable from 2023-04-03 in the closed study's cache and from 2024-01-02 in the 22-series macro frame, but the second condition needs a bias history that is not committed and the left side needs a growth series the collector never stores, so at most the high-volatility arm can be reconstructed.
factors.live_availability: Both inputs are read once per collector run with no per-field age and no stored regime label.

exports/usd_layer1_agent.json -> Build USD Input Pack (vix_level, vix_d1, vix_d5 and fed_bias exposed to the model)

factors.label: F10 Equity versus USD
factors.definition: The cross-asset read of equities against the dollar, gated by the same VIX regime: in calm markets a rising equity market is read as dollar-negative and a falling one as dollar-positive, and in stressed markets a falling equity market is read as dollar-positive. The rulebook's neutral-regime row, equities moving inside 16 to 25, is unhandled in code and falls into the same NEUTRAL branch as a missing input.

inputs.input: nq_d1_pct on 24h, else nq_d5_pct, and vix_level
inputs.source: Alpha Vantage GLOBAL_QUOTE on QQQ for the price; the one-day change is the vendor's own change-percent field and the five-day change is computed by historyPct against the collector's stored rows; VIXCLS for the gate
inputs.units: per cent change and index level
inputs.transform: sign of the equity change inside a VIX regime; the 24h arm prefers nq_d1_pct and falls back to nq_d5_pct when absent
inputs.lookback: one day on 24h; five stored rows on every other timeframe
inputs.cutoff: the quote is read at the pipeline run time and the daily change is the vendor's figure, not a change measured between the cutoff and the session end

factors.rule: VIX below 16 with NQ up reads BEARISH; VIX below 16 with NQ down BULLISH; VIX above 25 with NQ down BULLISH; every other combination NEUTRAL. No percentage threshold; only the sign of the change is read. Coded weight 1 at every timeframe; rulebook weight 2.
factors.missing_stale: A missing NQ change or a missing VIX level returns NEUTRAL with the evidence string 'Missing NQ/VIX'. The unhandled combinations, VIX above 25 with NQ up and the whole 16-to-25 band, also read NEUTRAL, and the payload does not distinguish an unhandled regime from absent data.
dependencies: An equity series whose change is measured against the cutoff rather than supplied by a vendor, and a decision on whether the factor should use the index or the ETF.
factors.overlap: F1 and F9 apply the same 25 and 16 thresholds, F6 reads the same risk appetite through gold, and the factor is the risk-appetite leg of the story F9's smile is built on.
factors.historical_availability: FRED NASDAQ100 is in the 22-series macro frame from 2024-01-02, but the live factor prices QQQ through Alpha Vantage, so the reconstructable series is not the collected one, and the vendor's change-percent field cannot be reproduced from a cached frame.
factors.live_availability: One row per collector run: the five-day arm counts stored rows and the one-day arm is the vendor's figure, with no age attached to either and no regime label stored alongside the call.
code_refs: exports/usd_layer1_agent.json -> Calculate USD Conviction, signals.F10: BEARISH when vix_level < 16 and the NQ change is positive, BULLISH when vix_level < 16 and it is negative, BULLISH when vix_level > 25 and it is negative, else NEUTRAL (weight 1 at every timeframe)
exports/usd_layer1_agent.json -> Calculate USD Conviction, nqDelta = nq_d1_pct on 24h when present, else nq_d5_pct

exports/usd_collector.json -> Normalise Market Snapshot: nq = alphaQuote(getNode('HTTP Request | NQ - Alpha Vantage')), nqD5Pct = historyPct(nq.price, 'nq_price', 4), nqD20Pct = historyPct(nq.price, 'nq_price', 19); equities_regime is stored from the VIX thresholds and read by no factor
